PullRequest.Title: chat: add user-perceived time to first progress telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Add `chat.userPerceivedTimeToFirstProgress` to measure UI submission entry to first meaningful progress while continuously visible, including Agents window new-session and new-chat composers.

- Qualifying progress is non-whitespace markdown/reasoning or a visible tool invocation (live or serialized).
- Hiding the widget/document ends measurement as `hidden` without stopping the request. Initially hidden/background submissions are ineligible, showing again never resumes timing, and focus loss alone does not end it.
- Agents composers hand off the original timer to the exact created response; session preparation and navigation are included without restarting the clock.
- Completion waits two animation frames and rechecks visibility/session identity. This is a render-boundary approximation, not a physical input or paint timestamp. Fork navigation is not measured.
- Queued sends are excluded from latency samples in both submission paths. Measurement has no duration cap and ends on progress or lifecycle events; provider/request timeouts are unchanged.
- Optional `[ChatTTFP] start` / `end` diagnostics use trace-level window logs.

## Event schema

Kusto: `monacoworkbench/chat.userperceivedtimetofirstprogress`. Ingested field names are lowercase.

### Measures

| Field | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeToFirstProgress` | ms | Duration to the render boundary; success only. |
| `timeToTermination` | ms | Duration until an unsuccessful observation ends; absent on success. |
| `windowVisible` | 0/1 | Source window visibility when the observation ends. |
| `windowFocused` | 0/1 | Source window focus when the observation ends. |

Missing timings are omitted, not zero. There is no full-response-duration measure.

### Properties

All properties are strings; context fields are omitted when unavailable.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | `success`, `cancelled`, `error`, `completedWithoutProgress`, `notDispatched`, `queued`, `navigated`, `hidden`, or `disposed`. |
| `requestPhase` | `first`, `followup`, or `unknown`, from this request's position in chat history; not a cold/warm process indicator. |
| `firstProgressKind` | `text`, `reasoning`, or `tool`; present only on successful observations. |
| `interactionKind` | `turn` (chat submission). |
| `requestId` | Submitted request ID. |
| `chatSessionId` | Session/peer-chat ID, excluding remote Agent Host connection authorities. |
| `agent` | Chat agent/participant ID. |
| `agentExtensionId` | Contributing extension ID. |
| `location` | Chat surface. |
| `model` | Selected model ID; Auto is not replaced with the resolved model. |
| `permissionLevel` | Selected tool-approval level. |
| `chatMode` | Telemetry mode name or ID. |
| `sessionType` | Normalized session type. |
| `harness` | Provider for remote Agent Host sessions; otherwise omitted. |

Unlike `agentHost.firstResponse` (#336704), this starts in the shared UI path and includes a render boundary rather than stopping at first response text.

## Validation

Client typecheck, transpilation, targeted ESLint, and whitespace checks passed. **141 focused tests per browser engine** (Chromium/WebKit/Firefox) and **138 Electron tests** cover queue exclusion, request phase, progress kind, continuous visibility, composer handoff, attribution, and cleanup.

For harness comparisons, use successful observations and compare matching request phases, progress kinds, and selected models. See the Checks tab for live CI status.

Scenarios.Scenario: Foreground submission from an existing chat widget through first visible response progress
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input validation and optional dictation shutdown precede the existing chatService.sendRequest dispatch. Response creation then installs an in-memory model listener; after qualifying progress is visible, two animation frames and one fixed-size telemetry emission complete the measurement. The telemetry does not await or delay provider completion, although its small final bookkeeping runs in the second frame callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the chat request to the selected agent/model provider through the existing chat service pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider dispatch per accepted non-queued request; queued requests retain the existing deferred dispatch behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sendRequest call and provider dispatch occurred before the diff; the new response observer is removed from request options before internal dispatch and does not add another provider call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains the dominant critical-path boundary before response progress can arrive.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record the fixed-schema chat.userPerceivedTimeToFirstProgress telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one small event per foreground interaction, including terminal unsuccessful observations; background submissions are excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No user-perceived first-progress telemetry event was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On success, fixed-size event construction/logging occurs in the second animation-frame callback; it does not await network upload or response completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chat history length affects one findIndex when the response is attached; streamed response updates are observed only until a terminal result, normally two frames after the first qualifying progress. No boundary call scales with history, token count, or widget count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One interaction is created per accepted foreground submission. Explicitly or implicitly queued sends terminate their measurement as queued; response listeners are attached only to the exact created response and are disposed on the first terminal result. Existing request serialization/queue behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Session telemetry context is computed from the current resource; provider/model caches and warm/cold behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds constant per-submit objects/listeners and one event, while preserving provider boundary count and queue semantics.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact synchronous telemetry-service cost and unusual pre-render streaming duration are not measured, but payload and event cardinality are fixed and listener cleanup is directly covered by the implementation and tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added work is bounded, the expensive provider boundary is not duplicated or moved, and observers are disposed on every traced terminal path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window new-session or new-chat-in-session composer handoff through session preparation and navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The foreground composer first runs the existing submit handler, then session preparation/createNewChat and provider.sendRequest. The new interaction object follows the exact session/chat/response through replacement and waits for the destination widget to expose progress; it does not add an await to preparation or dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load the chat model/session where required by Agent Host providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the same single acquire/load operation for the target chat as before the diff, with existing provider/session cache effects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already acquired or loaded the chat model before sending; only a UI callback is now forwarded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing preparation boundary remains before request dispatch; the callback pass-through performs no additional load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/prepare the session as needed and send the first or peer-chat request to the existing provider/model backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create-chat operation for a new session and one provider dispatch per accepted foreground send; peer chat uses one provider dispatch. No per-widget or per-session fan-out is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same preparation, createNewChat, and provider send sequence ran before the diff. onDidCreateResponse is passed through unchanged and stripped by ChatService before internal/provider serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing boundaries determine when a response can be created and progress can arrive.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record one fixed-size terminal first-progress telemetry event after handoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event for the single foreground composer send; no event object is created for background sends beyond existing unrelated telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It occurs only when the observation terminates and does not block session preparation or provider dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: In-memory observation scales with the number of simultaneously registered chat widgets and visible sessions, both application UI collections; scans are coalesced for visibility changes and all per-interaction listeners are released at termination. External calls remain one per logical send.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: NewChatInputWidget's existing _sending guard permits one foreground send from a composer at a time. Background sends create no interaction. Widget/session visibility checks are microtask-coalesced, and provider request concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing provider session/model caches remain authoritative. The interaction adds no cache or negative-cache state; cold session creation and warm committed-session sends retain their prior boundary behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the handoff implementation, management/provider call flow, callback stripping, and lifecycle tests that no additional subprocess, IPC, filesystem, or network operation is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish a hard maximum for open chat widgets or duration of remote preparation, but only one composer interaction is active and cleanup/queue exclusion is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: session/widget tracking is bounded to one foreground interaction, visibility checks are coalesced, and expensive preparation/dispatch cardinality is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Queued, hidden, cancelled, failed, navigated, or completed-without-progress submissions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The interaction terminates synchronously when the relevant lifecycle signal arrives, emits one termination event, and disposes response, widget, document, and animation-frame listeners. The underlying request behavior is intentionally unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit a fixed-size termination telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one event per attempted foreground interaction regardless of repeated terminal signals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These termination reasons were not emitted by this telemetry feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant local bookkeeping at termination; no provider cancellation or extra remote call is introduced by the measurement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant per user submission and does not follow deferred queue lifetime because queued measurements are immediately detached.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Queued submissions end observation immediately without awaiting the deferred request. Cancellation/error/hide/disposal paths are idempotent through the active flag, preventing duplicate telemetry or cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participation. Re-showing a hidden widget does not recreate or resume an interaction, so there is no repeated cold work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the active guard, disposal ownership, animation-frame cancellation, and focused lifecycle tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry backend batching cost is outside the inspected diff, but each payload is fixed-size and emitted once.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle or retention finding: every terminal path releases observers and pending frames, and queued work is not retained.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and traced normal chat, Agents composer handoff, provider dispatch, response streaming, rendering, telemetry, queueing, and cleanup. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; external boundary cardinality is unchanged and new work is bounded per foreground submission.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
